items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: Justin Adams, Placide Adams, and Mama Dolly Adams, and another brother, they come out of a traditional band setting but in the fifties they was playing modern jazz.

ctx.x: They was from across the river. Justin Adams, Placide Adams, and Mama Dolly Adams, and another brother, they come out of a traditional band setting but in the fifties they was playing modern jazz. And they all went back to playing, even the old lady, playing traditional music, that’s how they could make a living around New Orleans, you know when they made their comeback, they all started playing again. What about the Bocage family? You even heard of a trumpet player named Peter Bocage? Eddie Bocage?
I’ve seen it in the books, yeah.
